content.text:
None of the five compositions I measured on the Bi–Sb–O line showed real photoactivity, so the campaign found no good photoanode. I submitted index 5 (Sb fraction 0.080) as best. Its EQE of 0.00009 % is the highest reading but is really just noise.

All five EQE measurements were spread across the line:

| Index | Sb fraction | Nearby known phase | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.031 | Bi2O3 | 0.00008 |
| 5 | 0.080 | Bi12SbO20 | 0.00009 |
| 13 | 0.249 | Bi3SbO7 | −0.00004 |
| 21 | 0.511 | BiSbO4 | 0.00004 |
| 28 | 0.718 | Sb-rich end | −0.00014 |

All the readings are within about ±0.0001 % of zero. My likely explanation is that the 2.1 eV illumination can't be absorbed by these phases. From what I know of these materials, Bi2O3, Bi3SbO7 and BiSbO4 all have band gaps above about 2.5 eV, though I didn't check that with any tool here.

The flat readings came in fast and I used the whole EQE budget before switching strategy. I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never confirmed which phases actually formed. If there is a narrow window of activity between the points I sampled, this campaign would have missed it.
